:::{#thm-epe-decomposition}
#### Bias, variance and noise

Let $\mean$ be the [mean function](#def-mean-function) of the outcome given the covariate.
Suppose that, given $X_0 = x$,
the new outcome is $Y_0 = \mean(x) + \noise$,
where $\noise$, the noise in the outcome at $x$, has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar$,
and that $Y_0$ is independent of the random training set $\trainset$,
and that $\E{g\paren{x; \trainset}^2} < \infty$.
Then the [expected squared prediction error at $x$](#def-epe)
is the squared [bias](#def-prediction-bias)
of the prediction $g\paren{x; \trainset}$ as a prediction of $\mean(x)$,
plus its [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance),
plus $\varpar$:

$$
\epe{g}{n}{x} = \sqf{\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}}
+ \Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}} + \varpar.
$$ {#eq-epe-decomposition}

:::

::: proof

Write $\targeterrf{x} \eqdef \mean(x) - g\paren{x; \trainset}$,
the error of the prediction as an estimate of $\mean(x)$.
Given $X_0 = x$, the noise has mean 0 by @eq-mean-function and variance $\varpar$,
and it is independent of $g\paren{x; \trainset}$
because $Y_0$ is independent of $\trainset$;
hence it is independent of $\targeterrf{x}$,
because $\mean(x)$ is a constant.

First, the prediction error in terms of $\noise$ and $\targeterrf{x}$:

$$
\ba
Y_0 - g\paren{x; \trainset}
&= \paren{\mean(x) + \noise} - g\paren{x; \trainset}
&& \text{(definition of } Y_0 \text{)} \\
&= \noise + \paren{\mean(x) - g\paren{x; \trainset}}
&& \text{(reorder the terms of the sum)} \\
&= \noise + \targeterrf{x}
&& \text{(definition of } \targeterrf{x} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Next, expand the square and split the expectation, conditional on $X_0 = x$.
The last two steps use
[linearity of expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-linearity-expectation),
first for the expectation of a sum and then for a constant factor:

$$
\ba
\epe{g}{n}{x}
&= \E{\sqf{\paren{\noise + \targeterrf{x}}} \mid X_0 = x}
&& \text{(definition and the error above)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2 + 2 \noise \targeterrf{x} + \sqf{\targeterrf{x}}}
&& \text{(expand: } \paren{a + b}^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \text{)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + \E{2 \noise \targeterrf{x}} + \E{\sqf{\targeterrf{x}}}
&& \text{(expectation of a sum)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + 2\E{\noise \targeterrf{x}} + \E{\sqf{\targeterrf{x}}}
&& \text{(constant factor 2)}
\ea
$$

Each of the three terms is evaluated in turn.

- For the noise term, the
  [variance identity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-variance)
  gives $\varpar = \E{\noise^2} - \sqf{\E{\noise}}$,
  and $\E{\noise} = 0$, so $\E{\noise^2} = \varpar$.
- For the cross term,
  $\noise$ is independent of $\targeterrf{x}$,
  so the expectation of the product is the product of the expectations:

  $$
  \ba
  \E{\noise \targeterrf{x}}
  &= \E{\noise}\E{\targeterrf{x}}
  && \text{(independence)} \\
  &= 0 \cdot \E{\targeterrf{x}}
  && \text{(} \E{\noise} = 0 \text{)} \\
  &= 0
  && \text{(zero times a number)}
  \ea
  $$

- For the last term,
  the variance identity gives
  $\E{\sqf{\targeterrf{x}}} = \Var{\targeterrf{x}} + \sqf{\E{\targeterrf{x}}}$.
  The mean of $\targeterrf{x}$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \E{\targeterrf{x}}
  &= \E{\mean(x)} - \E{g\paren{x; \trainset}}
  && \text{(expectation of a difference)} \\
  &= \mean(x) - \E{g\paren{x; \trainset}}
  && \text{(} \mean(x) \text{ is a constant)} \\
  &= -\paren{\E{g\paren{x; \trainset}} - \mean(x)}
  && \text{(factor out } -1 \text{)} \\
  &= -\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}
  && \text{(definition of bias)}
  \ea
  $$

  so $\sqf{\E{\targeterrf{x}}} = \sqf{\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}}$,
  because $\sqf{\paren{-a}} = \sqf{a}$.
  The variance of $\targeterrf{x}$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \Var{\targeterrf{x}}
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{\targeterrf{x} - \E{\targeterrf{x}}}}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{-\paren{g\paren{x; \trainset} - \E{g\paren{x; \trainset}}}}}}
  && \text{(substitute; the constant } \mean(x) \text{ cancels)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{g\paren{x; \trainset} - \E{g\paren{x; \trainset}}}}}
  && \text{(} \sqf{\paren{-a}} = \sqf{a} \text{)} \\
  &= \Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)}
  \ea
  $$

Substituting the three terms into the expansion gives

$$
\ba
\epe{g}{n}{x}
&= \varpar + 2 \cdot 0 + \paren{\Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}} + \sqf{\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}}}
&& \text{(the three terms above)} \\
&= \sqf{\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}} + \Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}} + \varpar
&& \text{(drop } 2 \cdot 0 \text{, reorder the terms)}
\ea
$$

:::
